Manage precipitating factors

records.definition: Acute coronary syndrome with ST elevation on ECG (includes new onset LBBB). Diagnosis ideally confirmed within 10 minutes of first medical contact.

acs_definition: Angina at rest or lasting more than 20 minutes
Recent worsening of stable angina (crescendo) to CCS class III
New onset effort angina of less than 1 month in CCS class II/III
differential: Aortic dissection (unequal or absent peripheral pulses)

general_measures: Admit in ICU equipped with continuous ECG monitoring and defibrillation
Routine biochemistry and serial cardiac enzymes (troponin)
Oxygen if saturation less than 90 percent
Aspirin 325 mg, Clopidogrel 300 mg and Atorvastatin 80 mg

non_pci_capable: Transfer to PCI capable hospital if PCI can be performed within 120 minutes

time_based_pathways.action: Transfer to PCI capable hospital immediately

procedures.name: Routine early PCI after successful fibrinolysis
indications: Successful thrombolysis

procedures.name: Thrombolysis

timing_targets: Therapy to be started within 10 minutes preferably; within 30 minutes of diagnosis
procedures.agent_preference: Fibrin specific agent Tenecteplase, TPA or Reteplase; Streptokinase if fibrin-specific unavailable

absolute_contraindications_thrombolysis: Previous intracerebral hemorrhage or stroke of unknown etiology
Recent (within 1 month) major trauma, surgery or head injury
post_thrombolysis: ECG at 60-90 minutes after starting thrombolysis to assess success (greater than 50 percent ST settlement with pain relief)
If successful, transfer patient for PCI within 3-24 hours
If failed, transfer immediately to PCI capable hospital
Enoxaparin preferred over unfractionated heparin, continued till PCI or discharge

Urgent referral to higher centres with intensive care facilities

tertiary: Neuroimaging MRI/CT with contrast to rule out abscess or herniations; if abscess, emergency neurosurgical consultation for aspiration (open or stereotactic)

Non-resolution with oral antibiotics for ten days
Pointers of invasive fungal sinusitis (facial hypoesthesia, facial skin, palatal or turbinate discoloration)

clinical_preliminary: Anterior rhinoscopy: discharge, bleeding, crusting, polyposis
Oral examination: dental caries, post nasal drip, palatal discolouration
investigations.laboratory: Desirable in non-resolving or worsening cases despite antibiotic therapy
tests: Endoscopy for guided nasal swabs or KOH smear
CT PNS for suspected complications or non-resolving cases on antibiotics for 14 days

regimen: Oral antibiotics: amoxycillin or co-amoxyclav for 7-10 days; levofloxacin and azithromycin can be opted for patients intolerant or sensitive to penicillins
Topical budesonide or mometasone nasal spray once or twice a day for 2 weeks provides earlier symptomatic relief
Normal saline nasal washes help in clearing secretions and improve effect of topical medications
Topical or oral decongestant (oxymetazoline or pseudoephedrine) for 3-5 days relieves symptoms
Antihistaminics in patients with co-existing allergy

parenteral_antibiotic_indications: Non-resolution of symptoms with at least 7 days of oral antibiotics
Worsening of symptoms while on oral antibiotics
district: Surgical interventions to manage underlying anatomical conditions causing recurrent acute sinusitis such as DNS, adenoid hypertrophy, anatomical variations seen on CT
Ophthalmology referral for suspected intraorbital complications
Dental referral for suspected dental origin infection
Invasive fungal sinusitis: start antifungal medications, control underlying immunocompromising co-morbidity and consider debridement
tertiary: Cases of acute invasive fungal sinusitis, complicated acute bacterial sinusitis and patients with immunocompromised status may be referred for management

records.prior_auth_notes: CT PNS is authorised only for suspected complications or non-resolution after 14 days of antibiotics — a precise imaging gate. Symptoms under 7 days are by definition viral URI, which supports denial of antibiotic and imaging requests in that window.

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

records.definition: Symptoms persisting for more than 12 weeks: nasal obstruction, nasal discharge and facial pain or reduced sense of smell.
precipitating_factors_to_exclude: Occupational exposure to irritants or pollutants
Allergic rhinitis, aspirin sensitivity, asthma, laryngopharyngeal reflux, smoking
Adenoid hypertrophy, bottle feeding, passive smoking in children
Medications and hormones associated with nasal congestion: NSAIDs, antihypertensive, psychotropic drugs, prolonged use of topical nasal decongestants
red_flags: Orbital symptoms: periorbital edema/erythema, displaced globe, double or reduced vision (loss of green-red colour differentiation may be the first sign), ophthalmoplegia
Signs of meningitis or intracranial complications: fever with headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, altered sensorium, vomiting
Known diabetic, AIDS or on immunosuppressive medications (suspect invasive fungal sinusitis)

mild_moderate: For allergic rhinitis, antihistamines and nasal steroid spray to be given
Stretching exercises and yoga are very effective for nasal congestion
Topical (oxymetazoline, xylometazoline) and oral decongestants are associated with cardiovascular risks and rebound phenomenon, so careful patient selection and short course treatment to be followed
Intranasal steroid sprays for 6-8 weeks (fluticasone propionate, fluticasone furoate or mometasone) after discussing risk-benefit-cost issues with patient
treatment.escalation_rule: If no symptomatic relief to above treatment, perform nasal endoscopy and consider non-contrast CT of paranasal sinuses
purulent_discharge: Culture directed antibiotics to be considered
If culture is negative, empirical antibiotics (amoxycillin, co-amoxyclav, fluoroquinolone or roxithromycin) to be given for at least 2 weeks
Upper dental (particularly first molar) infection may cause maxillary sinusitis which is to be treated with metronidazole
nasal_polypi: Initial nasal steroid spray and subsequent endoscopic surgery is to be planned
Short course of oral steroid (prednisolone 0.5 mg/kg for 5-10 days) provides temporary relief in nasal obstruction in extensive polypi
Steroid therapy is not a replacement for surgery

allergy_rules: In all patients, especially in the presence of nasal polypi, rule out allergy or allergic rhinitis
Co-existing bronchial asthma needs to be treated
key_points: Identification of precipitating or exacerbating factors is the key to successful treatment outcome
Always rule out DNS or nasal polypi in CRS, as surgical treatment may be necessary for complete resolution of symptoms
Ensure adherence to nasal saline washes, regular physical activity and medications
Educate patients on correct technique of using steroid nasal sprays and nasal irrigation
Prolonged use of topical nasal decongestant beyond 5-7 days may cause rebound congestion and rhinitis medicamentosa and is to be strongly discouraged
records.prior_auth_notes: Functional endoscopic sinus surgery authorisation requires a documented 6-8 week intranasal steroid trial, failed symptomatic relief, nasal endoscopy and a CT PNS. Steroid therapy explicitly does not replace surgery in polypi — so a request for surgery in extensive polypi after steroid failure is supportable.

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

clinical_scenarios: Acute bleeding from the nose after physical trauma, barotrauma, nose picking or physical exertion
Acute bleeding from the nose in hypertensive or hematological disorders
Acute bleeding from the nose without any obvious cause

examination: Local examination by anterior rhinoscopy or endoscopy to look for source of bleeding
Little's area bleeder, clot or congestion
Sharp septal spur
Congested nasal mucosa as in URTI
General physical examination to evaluate cardiovascular, lower respiratory and neurological systems
clinical_criteria.systemic_assessment: Screen for coagulation disorders, anticoagulant medications, hematological malignancies
red_flags: Features suggestive of neoplasia: unilateral bleeding, nasal obstruction, visual or orbital symptoms, obvious mass lesion
Altered blood counts or coagulation profile

Recurrent profuse bleeding: consider juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma in teenage boys; aneurysmal bleeding especially following trauma to be ruled out by digital subtraction angiography; to be managed by appropriate treatment at tertiary level

desirable: CT scan with contrast in cases with no obvious cause or suspected benign or malignant lesion

stepwise_management: Ensure patent airway and avoid aspiration by head down or lateral positioning
Restore hemodynamic stability by intravenous fluid replacement or transfusion
Bidigital compression of nose for 10 minutes in Trotter's position (cotton pledgets soaked in 4 percent xylocaine with adrenaline may be used)
Short term tab labetalol will take care of uncontrolled hypertension
Chemical or electrocauterization of bleeder in Little's area
Tamponade of bleeders by anterior nasal packing or epistaxis balloon
Posterior nasal packing if bleeding is not controlled with above measures
Antibiotic prophylaxis and hospitalization is recommended after nasal packing
H2 blockers or PPI to be given in case of blood aspiration to avoid gastritis
Persisting bleeding despite nasal packing: consider arterial ligation (sphenopalatine or anterior ethmoidal artery)
Selective embolization is an alternative to surgery

procedures.name: Arterial ligation (sphenopalatine or anterior ethmoidal)
indications: Persisting bleeding despite nasal packing

procedures.name: Selective embolization
indications: Alternative to surgery where bleeding persists despite packing

procedures.name: Digital subtraction angiography
indications: Recurrent profuse bleeding with suspected aneurysmal bleeding especially following trauma

clinical_pearls: Epistaxis in children is almost always anterior and from Little's area, consequent to mucosal drying by dry air
Epistaxis in adults is often related to hypertension and arises posteriorly from the posterior end of inferior turbinate
Initial non-invasive methods may suffice in a large majority of patients
follow_up: Continued nasal lubrication for 2 weeks with liquid paraffin
Repeat anterior rhinoscopy or endoscopy to know or confirm the cause of bleeding
Oral hematinics to be considered if needed
quality_metrics: Improvement in hemoglobin level over a period of time
records.prior_auth_notes: Arterial ligation and embolization both require documented failure of nasal packing — a clean stepwise-escalation rule. Contrast CT is reserved for no-obvious-cause or suspected mass lesion cases.

records.condition: Hearing Impairment in Paediatric Age Group (0-12 years)

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

records.definition: Disabling hearing impairment (31 or more dB HL in better ear) may affect language development and learning outcomes and hence needs urgent intervention.
when_to_suspect: Parental concern about delayed speech, language and developmental delay
Exposure to ototoxic drugs, hyperbilirubinemia requiring exchange transfusion, or neonatal ICU stay for more than 3 days
In-utero infections (CMV, rubella, syphilis, herpes, toxoplasmosis)
Syndromes (neurofibromatosis) or neurodegenerative disorders (Hunter syndrome, Friedreich ataxia) associated with hearing loss
Post-natal infection known to cause hearing loss (meningitis)
Recurrent or persistent (3 months or more) middle ear disease
Chemotherapy or radiotherapy to head and neck
red_flags_urgent_evaluation: 6 months: no head turning to the side of calling
1 year: no babbling or speech like sound production
1.5 years: not saying mama, papa, dada or other names
2 years: not pointing to pictures or body parts when named, or speaking less than 10 words
3 years: does not understand action words, not asking for things by names, or not speaking small sentences
At any age: has regressed or lost previously acquired speech or language milestones
universal_screening: Community based hearing screening may be co-ordinated with immunization schedule
All children who fail preliminary screen to undergo detailed evaluation at health care facility

essential: Clinical examination to look for ear canal deformities, tympanic membrane and middle ear status by otoscopy or otoendoscopy
Age appropriate audiological or behavioral observation tests in a soundproof room by audiologist or ENT specialist
Tympanic membrane mobility test or tympanometry

common_causes: Middle ear fluid associated with adenoid hypertrophy or cold climate
Sensorineural hearing loss due to various causes as indicated

conductive_hearing_loss: Wax removal under direct vision by ENT specialist relieves hearing impairment
Appropriate surgery is to be planned for tympanic membrane perforation

Middle ear fluid (OME) may be associated with adenotonsillar disease which needs to be treated. Initially medical treatment, and surgery to be considered for OME persisting for more than 3 months or earlier in the presence of speech and language delay
For non-surgical candidates or delayed surgical management, amplification by hearing aid to be reinforced in bilateral conductive hearing loss
sensorineural_hearing_loss: Appropriate amplification, preferential seating in classroom
Periodic evaluation for hearing aid users for mould fitting and amplification settings
Screening for developmental delay by pediatrician or psychologist

phc: Referral if initial evaluation is suggestive of hearing loss
Follow up of rehabilitated or treated patients
district: Audiometric evaluation by audiologist or otolaryngologist
Hearing aid dispensing (mould fitting and hearing aid programming)
Rehabilitation by speech therapist
Appropriate surgery for conductive hearing loss
Training programme for parents of hearing impaired children to enhance pre-school language development
tertiary: Surgical intervention options: cochlear implant or bone anchored hearing aid as per ADIP guidelines
Interdisciplinary team based interventions in children with multiple disabilities

procedures.name: Cochlear implant
indications: As per ADIP (Assistance to Disabled Persons) guidelines

procedures.name: Bone anchored hearing aid (BAHA)
indications: As per ADIP guidelines

procedures.name: Surgery for otitis media with effusion
indications: OME persisting for more than 3 months, or earlier in the presence of speech and language delay

quality_metrics: Short term: quality of amplification using electroacoustic objective measures and culturally appropriate subjective questionnaire tools
Long term (desirable): use community based rehabilitation matrix based measurement for ensuring holistic rehabilitation
records.prior_auth_notes: Cochlear implant is the highest-cost item in this STW and is explicitly deferred to national ADIP guidelines, so a payer rule should cross-reference those rather than the STW alone. Grommet/OME surgery has a clean 3-month persistence threshold with an early-intervention exception for speech delay.

records.definition: Rapidly progressive bacterial infections which spread along facial planes and spaces of head and neck region. They may be fatal unless emergently treated. Most of these infections are secondary to dental infection.

presentation: Acute onset of pain and swelling in the neck with fever, malaise, trismus and dysphagia
Extension along spaces to involve multiple deep neck spaces is frequent and may extend to parotid space, masticator space, temporal space, visceral vascular (carotid) space
Cervical space infection may spread inferiorly to the anterior mediastinum and posteriorly along prevertebral space
Tubercular cold abscess involves the same anatomical spaces but would not display inflammatory signs or rapid progression
examination: Airway assessment to rule out stridor or respiratory compromise
Look for signs of dehydration
Monitor temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, BP, and signs of sepsis or septic shock
Oral cavity examination to check jaw opening, condition of teeth and floor of mouth
Oropharyngeal examination to check for inflamed medially displaced tonsil and uvula and bulge in lateral pharyngeal wall
Palpation of neck for lymph nodes, cellulitis, abscess or subcutaneous crepitus
Cranial nerve examination to rule out lower cranial nerve palsies
clinical_criteria.systemic_assessment: Screen for diabetes mellitus, HIV infection, agranulocytosis and immunosuppressive therapy or chemotherapy. Signs of inflammation may be less marked and disease course may be more rapidly progressive in immunocompromised patients.
red_flags_referral: Subcutaneous crepitus and skin discolouration or blisters suggest necrotizing fasciitis
Facial puffiness suggestive of venous thrombosis

essential: Contrast enhanced CT scan of head and neck is the standard in evaluation of neck space infections

If CT scan facility is not available: lateral X-ray neck (prevertebral soft tissue thickening greater than 7 mm at the level of C2 or greater than two-thirds of the width of the vertebral body at C6 is highly suggestive of retropharyngeal abscess)
Ultrasound neck can suggest abscess and guide aspiration attempts
Blood: total and differential leukocyte count, blood sugar, urea
Abscess cultures with gram stain to direct antimicrobial therapy; anaerobic culture when available

phc: Cautiously assess the airway; if found compromised, do endotracheal intubation or consider tracheotomy
Immediately gain an IV access for hydration, broad spectrum antibiotics and pain killers
Transfer the patient to hospital with facility for surgical drainage
district: Hospitalization as an emergency for close watch and intensive management

Airway management: in progressive disease, in view of impending airway compromise, consider securing the airway early. During acute respiratory difficulty, tracheostomy should be done if intubation is difficult.
Correction of fluid and electrolyte imbalance
Antibiotics: early and aggressive IV antibiotic therapy with a combination of crystalline penicillin, aminoglycoside and metronidazole or clindamycin is preferred
Incision and drainage: peritonsillar abscess is drained intraorally; all other abscesses are drained via an external approach

procedures.name: Incision and drainage
indications: Necrotizing fasciitis
Abscess formation
No response to antibiotics over 48-72 hours
Deterioration despite antibiotics over 24 hours
Airway compromise or impending airway compromise
Mediastinal spread
Vascular complication like venous thrombosis
procedures.approach: Peritonsillar abscess drained intraorally; all others via external approach

procedures.name: Tracheostomy
indications: Acute respiratory difficulty where intubation is difficult

follow_up: Consider cold tonsillectomy for patients with history of multiple episodes of tonsillar abscess
quality_metrics: Complete resolution of infection and follow up to ensure no recurrence
Treatment of initial cause of infection in tooth or tonsil
records.prior_auth_notes: Contrast CT head and neck is designated the standard investigation, so it should approve readily. Incision and drainage has a seven-item indication list including a specific 48-72 hour antibiotic non-response threshold.

external_ear: Serous or purulent discharge with significant tenderness of external ear amidst edema: localized pus is furunculosis, generalized is acute otitis externa denoting Staphylococcus or Pseudomonas infection
Thick discharge with itching usually in hot or humid climate: otomycosis (Candida shows white spores, Aspergillus black spores)
Scanty serous discharge and itching with desquamated debris in ear canal: eczematous otitis externa
middle_ear: URI with severe ear pain (in children manifested as inconsolable crying and ear tugging), relieved with episode of mucopurulent blood stained otorrhoea: resolving acute otitis media

Mucopurulent discharge more than 12 weeks: chronic suppurative otitis media (CSOM). Active: otorrhoea in last 12 weeks. Inactive: no otorrhoea in last 12 weeks. Safe type: central perforation and total perforation. Unsafe type: cholesteatoma and granulation.

Recurrent painless profuse mucopurulent discharge with pale granulations or multiple perforations unresponsive to antibiotics: tubercular otitis media should be suspected and needs biopsy confirmation
Bloody otorrhoea following trauma: traumatic perforation
Acute onset bloody discharge with neural deficits or neck nodes: neoplasia
Watery otorrhoea, may be associated with trauma: CSF otorrhoea

clinical: Otoscopy as part of complete ENT examination by primary physician (tele-otoscopy interpreted by physician)
Hearing evaluation by conversation, whisper or tuning fork tests
tests: Routine hemogram including blood sugar (fasting and postprandial)
CT or MRI in suspected complications
Soft tissue X-ray nasopharynx to examine adenoid enlargement in children
Culture and sensitivity of aural secretions

red_flags_referral: High grade fever, dizziness and toxic appearance
Severe headache with neck stiffness, vomiting or altered sensorium
Diabetic with severe deep seated ear pain or neural deficits (skull base osteomyelitis)
Physical trauma with bloody or watery discharge (suspected CSF leak)

treatment_by_diagnosis.regimen: Oral ciprofloxacin or amoxycillin clavulanic acid combination for 7-10 days (2 weeks maximum) and analgesics. Ichthammol glycerine (1:9) packing of external auditory canal in moderate to severe edema. Refer pus pointing furuncle to district hospital.
Ciprofloxacin ear drops with steroid combination
Oral amoxicillin, erythromycin or clarithromycin for 10 days. With no response in 3 days start amoxycillin clavulanic acid combination for 10 days. Refer to district hospital if no resolution.
Referral to district hospital for surgery
Ciprofloxacin ear drops with dry mopping and referral to district hospital for surgery. A course of oral antibiotics may be prescribed in case of persistent otorrhoea after topical antibiotics.
Topical antibiotics for otorrhoea if any and maintain ear dry till healing complete
Start intravenous amoxycillin clavulanic acid combination and refer to district hospital

district: Surgical interventions except neurosurgical interventions (incision and drainage, tympanoplasty, mastoidectomy)
Biopsy in suspected neoplasm
Medical management of medical co-morbidities such as diabetes, tuberculosis, meningismus or meningitis
tertiary: Surgical management particularly of intracranial complications including neurosurgical interventions

patient_education: Proper technique of ear mopping, contralateral lie for 10 minutes following instillation of drops and avoiding water entry (ear-plugs during bathing)
Ensure adequate immunization (measles, H. influenzae, pneumococcus) in recurrent acute otitis media and adopt correct posture during breastfeeding while avoiding bottle feeding
Pus culture sensitivity to guide antibiotic regime in recurrent or complicated cases
Patient education to refrain from indigenous (oil, hot water, acid) ear treatments
records.prior_auth_notes: Tympanoplasty and mastoidectomy are district-level procedures indicated for CSOM (active after topical therapy, or inactive). The 12-week discharge threshold defines CSOM and is the documentation requirement for surgical authorisation.

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

clinical_scenarios: Acute onset of throat pain with or without fever, tonsillo-pharyngeal exudates, odynophagia and tender cervical lymphadenopathy is typically seen in bacterial pharyngitis; streptococcal (GABHS) pharyngitis is the commonest cause of bacterial pharyngitis
Rhinitis, conjunctivitis, skin or mucosal rashes point towards a viral etiology; pharyngitis and sore throat may be the initial symptoms in epidemics of flu
Sore throat followed by high grade fever, cough, drooling, lymphadenopathy, breathing difficulty suggest epiglottitis or laryngotracheobronchitis especially in pediatric patients
An adherent membrane extending beyond the tonsillar confines with toxaemia suggests diphtheria
Pharyngitis with generalized lymphadenopathy is consistent with infectious mononucleosis
Smoking and GERD are common causes of non-infective pharyngitis

thresholds.action: Not to be treated with antibiotics

thresholds.interpretation: Require lab tests to confirm GABHS infection
thresholds.action: Treat with antibiotics only if antigen testing or throat swab culture is positive
Treat with antibiotics without waiting for antigen testing or cultures

preliminary_examination: Temperature chart: fever is usually absent or low-grade in viral pharyngitis
Check for vitals and signs of dehydration due to compromised oral intake from odynophagia
Complete oral and oropharyngeal examination with tongue depressor
Palpate for cervical and generalized lymphadenopathy
Rheumatic fever and acute glomerulonephritis are potential systemic complications of streptococcal pharyngitis
Hepatosplenomegaly can be found in infectious mononucleosis

A sandpapery scarlatiniform rash may be seen in GABHS infection whereas maculopapular rashes are seen with various viral infections and with infectious mononucleosis empirically treated with penicillin
red_flags: Purulent productive cough with tachypnea suggestive of lower respiratory tract infection
Tonsillar membrane going beyond its confines

essential: Routine hemogram including total and differential leukocyte counts
Peripheral smear to look for atypical lymphocytes (seen in infectious mononucleosis)
desirable: Lab tests to rule out EB virus, Coxsackie virus, herpes virus, fungal or gonococcal pharyngitis

phc_primary: Assess the patient for signs of toxicity, epiglottitis or oropharyngeal abscess
Ensure vitals and hydration of the patient
Saltwater gargle, warm liquids, and rest may be helpful in relieving symptoms
Ibuprofen or paracetamol is recommended for analgesia
Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day in 2-3 doses orally for 10 days is the first choice for GABHS infection; for patients sensitive to penicillin group, erythromycin or azithromycin is the antibiotic of choice
Parenteral antibiotics (ceftriaxone or cefotaxime) and steroids are to be started when the airway is compromised due to suspected epiglottitis or croup
district: Management of complications: deep neck space infection, diphtheria, epiglottitis, croup

records.tonsillectomy_criteria: Recurrent tonsillitis episodes need to be evaluated for tonsillectomy: more than 7 episodes in previous year, or 5 per year in last two years, or 3 per year in last 3 years
records.prior_auth_notes: Two hard rules here: Centor score determines antibiotic authorisation (0-1 no antibiotics; 2-3 requires positive test; 4 empiric), and tonsillectomy has an exact episode-frequency threshold (7/1yr, 5/yr x2, 3/yr x3) that is directly codeable as an approve/deny rule.

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

records.definition: Acute onset of fever (7 days or less) with altered sensorium and/or new onset of seizures, excluding simple febrile seizures.

additional_history: Rash, vesicles, past history of chicken pox
Residence of child rural or urban, endemic for cerebral malaria, any epidemic of AES in neighborhood
Animal contact, insect bite, dog bite
Drug or toxin exposure, enquire for presence of any drugs at home
Pre-morbid developmental or neurological status of the child

essential: CSF examination (cytology, biochemistry, culture, AFB staining, Gene Xpert)
desirable: CSF PCR for herpes simplex encephalitis
optional: PCR viral testing of other samples (throat swab, nasopharyngeal aspirates, stool)
Blood tandem mass spectrometry and urine gas chromatography

records.lumbar_puncture_rule: Lumbar puncture is contraindicated, or neuroimaging must be obtained before lumbar puncture, when any of the listed features is present

management_steps.title: Rapid assessment and stabilization
actions: Establish and maintain airway; intubate if GCS less than 8, impaired airway reflexes, abnormal respiratory pattern, signs of raised intracranial pressure, SpO2 less than 92 percent despite high flow oxygen, or fluid refractory shock
Ventilation, oxygenation
Circulation: establish IV access, take samples, fluid bolus if in circulatory failure (20 mL/kg normal saline), inotropes if required
Identify signs of cerebral herniation or raised ICP
Treat fever and hypothermia
Treat ongoing seizures with benzodiazepine followed by phenytoin loading

management_steps.title: Empirical treatment
management_steps.rule: Must be started if CSF cannot be done or report will take time and patient is sick
actions: Ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses for 10-14 days
Acyclovir in all suspected sporadic viral encephalitis: 3 months to 12 years 500 mg/m2 8 hourly (minimum 21 days); over 12 years 10 mg/kg 8 hourly (14-21 days in confirmed cases)

Artesunate combination therapy, stop if peripheral smear and rapid diagnostic test are negative: 3 mg/kg in child under 20 kg and 2.4 mg/kg in child over 20 kg IV/IM at 0, 12 and 24 hours, followed by once daily parenteral or oral for 3-7 days
management_steps.stopping_rule: If therapy was started empirically stop acyclovir if an alternative diagnosis is confirmed, or HSV PCR of CSF is negative on two occasions 24-48 hours apart and MRI imaging is not suggestive of herpes simplex encephalitis

management_steps.title: Supportive care and treatment
actions: Maintain euglycemia, hydration and control fever
Treat raised intracranial pressure, mild head-end elevation 15-30 degrees
Treat seizures; give anticonvulsant if history of seizures, GCS less than 8, or features of raised ICP
Steroids: pulse steroids (methylprednisolone) in children with suspected acute disseminated encephalomyelitis or autoimmune encephalitis

management_steps.title: Prevention or treatment of complications and rehabilitation
actions: Physiotherapy, posture change, prevent bed sores and exposure keratitis
Watch for complications: aspiration pneumonia, nosocomial infections, coagulation disturbances
Nutrition: early feeding
Psychological support to patient and family

raised_icp_management: Intubate if GCS less than 8, evidence of herniation, or irregular respirations and inability to maintain airway
Signs of impending herniation: hyperventilate to a target PaCO2 of 30-35 mmHg
Initial bolus of mannitol 0.25 g/kg, then 0.25 g/kg every 6 hours as per requirement up to 48 hours
In the presence of hypotension, hypovolemia and renal failure: hypertonic (3 percent) saline preferable to mannitol, 0.1-1 mL/kg/hr by infusion; serum sodium to be targeted to 145-155 mEq/L
Administer nebulized lignocaine prior to endotracheal tube suctioning
seizure_treatment: First line: IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg or midazolam 0.2 mg/kg or diazepam 0.3 mg/kg; if no IV access, IM midazolam 0.2 mg/kg
Second line: injection phenytoin 20 mg/kg in normal saline at 1 mg/kg/min
Refractory status: transfer to PICU for midazolam infusion 1-18 microgram/kg/min
If ICU facilities not available: sodium valproate 20 mg/kg, levetiracetam 20-40 mg/kg, or phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg
referral_criteria: All patients need to be admitted

Refer to tertiary care facility with PICU and mechanical ventilation if: Glasgow Coma Scale less than 8, abnormal breathing pattern, shock not responding to fluid bolus, decerebrate or decorticate posturing, or seizures persisting despite benzodiazepine and phenytoin
discharge_criteria: Hemodynamically stable
Improvement in consciousness
Afebrile
Has started eating and drinking orally
Seizures have subsided
Parents have been explained the supportive care and physiotherapy to be continued at home
records.prior_auth_notes: Acyclovir has an explicit discontinuation rule (two negative HSV PCRs 24-48 hours apart plus non-suggestive MRI), which supports retrospective length-of-therapy review. Neuroimaging before LP is mandated by five listed features.

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

clinical_criteria.when_to_suspect: Fever and two of the following: nausea, vomiting, rash, myalgia, headache, retro orbital pain, arthralgia, hemorrhagic manifestations — in a patient who lives in or has travelled to a dengue endemic area
warning_signs: Clinical fluid accumulation: pleural effusion, ascites
Mucosal bleed: melena, epistaxis, gum bleed
Shock (DSS): weak rapid pulse, pulse pressure less than 20 mmHg, hypotension, cold clammy skin, restlessness

optional: USG guided measurement of collapsibility of IVC for monitoring hypovolemia

referral_criteria: Rising PCV and thrombocytopenia without clinical symptoms

protocol: Ringer's lactate or normal saline 10 ml/kg/hr
Assess after every hour by checking HR, RR, BP, CVP and PCV
If improvement: RL 5-7 ml/kg for 1-2 hr, then on further improvement RL 3-5 ml/kg/hr, continue IV fluids till stable for 24 hours, then observe 24 hours and discharge if criteria fulfilled
If no improvement: RL 10-15 ml/kg/hr, reassess at second hour; if still no improvement RL 15 ml/kg/hr, reassess at third hour; if still no improvement colloids 10 ml/kg/hr
If still no improvement: look for anemia, acidosis, myocardial dysfunction and treat accordingly

hypotensive_shock.definition: Tachypnea, tachycardia, hypotension, peripheral pulses not palpable
protocol: 20 ml/kg crystalloid or colloid in 15 minutes
Assess shock by monitoring HR, RR, BP, PCV and CVP
If improvement: gradually decrease infusion rate — 10 ml/kg/hr for 1-2 hr, 7 ml/kg for 2-3 hrs, 5 ml/kg for 2-4 hrs, 3 ml/kg for 2-4 hrs, stop at 48 hours
If no improvement and PCV increased: colloids 10-20 ml/kg
If no improvement and PCV decreased: blood transfusion
If still no improvement: look for blood loss, acidosis, cardiac dysfunction and treat accordingly

shock_management.referral_rule: In case of shock, start bolus and arrange for urgent referral with continuous monitoring by a health professional to facilities with a PICU

packed_red_cells: Loss of blood (overt blood) 10 percent or more of total blood volume
platelets: Prophylactic platelet transfusion if platelet count less than 10,000/cumm

clinical: Improvement in clinical status: general well-being, appetite, haemodynamic status, urine output, respiratory distress
discharge_criteria.rule: ALL of the following conditions must be present

records.prior_auth_notes: Platelet transfusion has a hard prophylactic threshold of under 10,000/cumm — the single most commonly over-utilised service in dengue and a high-value automated denial rule. Packed cell and FFP indications are similarly closed lists.

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

records.definition: More than 3 loose or watery stools per day. Acute diarrhea less than 14 days; persistent diarrhea more than 14 days; dysentery is blood in stools.

dehydration_classification.criteria: 2 or more of: lethargy or unconscious, sunken eyes, not able to drink or drinking poorly, skin pinch goes back very slowly
2 or more of: restless or irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly or thirsty, skin pinch goes back slowly
Not enough signs to classify some or severe dehydration

fluids: Give extra fluids (as much as child will take) until diarrhea stops
Use WHO ORS after each loose stool in addition to usual fluid intake
Frequent small sips with spoon or cup; if child vomits wait 10 minutes then continue slowly
suitable_home_fluids: Vegetable or chicken soup with salt and clean water
feeding: Infants on breast feed to continue more frequent breast feeding than usual
Those not on breast feed to continue their usual milk feed or formula at least once in 3 hours
Give age appropriate foods to children over 6 months based on their pre-illness feeding pattern

plan_b_some_dehydration.protocol: Manage in clinic or daycare facility with recommended amount of ORS (75 ml/kg) over 4 hour period. After 4 hours reassess the child, classify dehydration and select appropriate plan.

protocol: Ideal fluid is Ringer lactate solution or normal saline (DNS in malnourished)
If child can drink, give ORS by mouth while the drip is set up
Assess heart rate, respiratory rate, BP, capillary refill time, consciousness and recognize early shock
monitoring: Reassess every 15-30 minutes till a strong radial pulse is present, then every hour
If hydration status is not improving, give IV drip more rapidly
After 6 hours in infants and 3 hours in older patients, evaluate for dehydration and choose the appropriate plan
Give ORS about 5 ml/kg/hour as soon as the child can drink, usually after 3-4 hours in infants or 1-2 hours in children
Observe for 6 hours after the child has been fully rehydrated

dysentery_treatment: Ciprofloxacin 15 mg/kg twice a day and reassess after 2 days; if improvement complete 3 days of treatment
If no improvement, cefixime 10 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses; reassess after 2 days; if better complete 3-5 days
If stool routine positive for amoebiasis: metronidazole 10 mg/kg/dose 8 hourly for 7 days (10 days in severe cases)
records.cholera_treatment: If prevalence of cholera: doxycycline single dose 300 mg or tetracycline 12.5 mg/kg 4 times a day for 3 days. For young children erythromycin 12.5 mg/kg 4 times a day for 3 days.
records.vomiting_treatment: Ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg/dose IV or oral in addition to rehydration therapy

suspected_cholera: Preferable: stool for hanging drop and stool culture
dysentery_no_response_2_days: Preferable: stool culture and stool routine for trophozoites of amoeba
persistent_diarrhea: Preferable: stool routine microscopy, urine routine microscopy, urine culture, sepsis screen

referral_criteria: Hypernatremic (Na greater than 145 mmol/L) or hyponatremic dehydration (Na less than 135 mmol/L)
Dysentery with age under 1 year, measles in past 6 weeks, dehydration or sick appearance
Dysentery with no improvement on antibiotics
Persistent diarrhea with serious systemic infection such as pneumonia or sepsis, infants under 4 months of age, or when there is no improvement with treatment over 5 days
discharge_criteria: Sufficient rehydration indicated by weight gain and/or clinical status
IV fluids no longer needed
Oral intake equal to or greater than losses
Medical follow-up available
records.prior_auth_notes: Antibiotics are only authorised for dysentery, cholera and specific parasitic findings — routine antibiotic use in acute watery diarrhea is not supported. Zinc dosing is age-banded. IV fluids require documented severe dehydration by the two-sign rule.

records.definition: Core (rectal) temperature 38.0 C (100.4 F) or more, or axillary temperature more than 37.5 C.

investigation_tiers.essential: If fever less than 72 hours and child not looking sick: no investigations. If fever more than 72 hours: TLC, DLC, peripheral smear for leukocyte morphology, malarial parasite and platelet count
desirable: NS1 antigen and dengue IgM antibody

investigation_tiers.scenario: Less than 7 days with localizing symptoms
Less than 7 days with non specific symptoms
desirable: NS1 antigen and dengue IgM antibody

investigation_tiers.scenario: More than 7 days, fever alone or without localizing symptoms
investigation_tiers.essential: All essential and desirable investigations from prior tiers, additionally consider Widal test
optional: Ultrasonography of abdomen, chest, pericardium, joints, abscess, lymph node clusters, parotid gland for microscopy

investigation_tiers.scenario: More than 7 days with localizing symptoms
investigation_tiers.essential: All investigations mentioned in the prior tiers
desirable: Serology for Brucella, CMV, herpes, Japanese encephalitis
CT scan in deep seated abscess or lung abscess

records.investigation_rule: Perform investigations only where the result impacts management

clues: Membrane over tonsils or pharynx: diphtheria
Red maculopapular rash: measles, rubella, dengue
Fine generalized maculopapular rash with systemic dysfunction or shock: meningococcemia
Itchy erythematous macules evolving to clear vesicles: varicella
Arthritis: consider chikungunya, acute rheumatic fever, juvenile idiopathic arthritis
Strawberry red tongue, skin peeling, lymphadenopathy, conjunctival injection: Kawasaki disease

management_steps.title: Initial assessment and stabilization
actions: Decrease body temperature with paracetamol 15 mg/kg by any route and/or hydrotherapy
Manage any life-threatening issue
Consider first dose antibiotic in suspected meningitis, severe pneumonia, or severe malnutrition
Consider anti-malarial in suspected malaria

management_steps.title: Consider hospitalization for observation or management
criteria: All neonates
Young infants with toxic appearance
Severe malnutrition, toxic appearance, inability to feed, lethargy, irritability, dehydration
More than 14 days illness without diagnosis
Any reason deemed by the treating physician

management_steps.title: Consider referral to tertiary care centre (after appropriate stabilization)
criteria: Need for intensive care
Complex multi-system disease
Confirmed complications of the primary illness

management_steps.title: Empiric management
rules: Consider based on likely diagnosis, sickness status and availability of investigation facilities
Empiric treatment should be tailored based on subsequently available investigation reports and local antimicrobial sensitivity
Anti tuberculosis treatment should not be started on empiric basis except in suspected tuberculous meningitis

management_steps.title: Consider discharge when
criteria: Afebrile more than 48 hours or fever is showing defervescence
Feeding well
Presenting symptoms (in addition to fever) resolved or resolving
Physician is satisfied that further care can be continued on ambulatory basis
Duration of IV antibiotic therapy is completed

records.prior_auth_notes: A duration-and-localisation matrix determines which investigations are authorised: nothing under 72 hours in a well child; blood culture and serology at 3-7 days; imaging, bone marrow and PET only beyond 7 days. This is one of the most directly implementable diagnostic-utilisation rule sets in the volume. Empiric anti-TB therapy is explicitly not authorised except in suspected TBM.

records.condition: Sepsis and Septic Shock in Children (2-59 months)

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

records.definition: Sepsis to be suspected in children with any infection (fever with or without rashes, pneumonia, diarrhoea) who are at risk of life threatening organ dysfunction.

vital_sign_thresholds: Pulse volume: high volume as well as low volume or feeble pulse
Heart rate and respiratory rate outside the age range
Capillary refilling time greater than 3 seconds
Pulse oximetry saturation less than 95 percent
Blood pressure: systolic BP less than 70 in children under 1 year; in children over 1 year systolic BP less than 70 plus (age in years times 2)
clinical_criteria.fast_pulse_definition: Heart rate greater than 180 in children under 12 months; greater than 120 in children over 12 months
clinical_criteria.poor_perfusion_definition: Fast pulse, cold peripheries, poor pulse volume, capillary refill time greater than 3 seconds

initial: Start oxygen with face mask at 4-6 L/min, or hood at 8-10 L, or nasal prongs 1-2 L/min if not available, to maintain SpO2 greater than 95 percent
Give first dose of antibiotics within first one hour
fluid_protocol: Give 20 ml/kg of normal saline fluid bolus over 20-30 minutes
Repeat bolus of 20 ml/kg over 30 minutes, with careful monitoring for hepatomegaly, oxygen saturation and crepitations in chest; if any of these appear then stop fluids

If there is improvement after first bolus and history of diarrhea is present: give 70 ml/kg over 5 hours in infants and over 2.5 hours in a child with hypovolemic shock; give additional fluids if losses continue
Start maintenance fluid in case of other illness
management.inotropes: If shock persists: start injection adrenaline infusion at 0.1 microgram/kg/min and refer to higher centre. Adrenaline preparation: 0.3 times body weight in mg in 50 ml normal saline or 5 percent dextrose at 1 ml/hr gives 0.1 microgram/kg/min.
antibiotics: Over 3 months: injection ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses
Under 3 months: injection cefotaxime 200 mg/kg divided 6-8 hourly plus injection gentamicin 5-7.5 mg/kg single dose per day
If soft tissue infection: consider injection cloxacillin 200 mg/kg divided 6 hourly or injection amoxicillin-clavulanic acid 30 mg/kg/dose 8 hourly

when_to_suspect: History of forehead sweating or suck-rest-suck cycle
cardiac_failure_caution.action: If suspected, be careful in giving fluid bolus

referral_criteria: Shock does not improve after second fluid bolus
Before referral counsel the parents and inform referring facility
complications: Respiratory failure (excessive increase in respiratory rates and inability to maintain saturation above 94 percent with oxygen): non-invasive CPAP/BIPAP or invasive ventilation
Congestive heart failure: dobutamine or milrinone infusion and furosemide
Infections at other sites: explore and treat accordingly
discharge_criteria: Completion of antibiotics as per culture sensitivity
Adequate urine output greater than 1 ml/kg/hr
Afebrile for 48 hours
Vitals within normal limit for age
Good oral intake
records.prior_auth_notes: Antibiotics within the first hour is a quality metric supporting concurrent review. The two-bolus-then-refer rule and the fluid-overload stop signs (hepatomegaly, desaturation, crepitations) are auditable safety checks.

diagnostic_criteria.sam: MUAC less than 11.5 cm, or weight-for-height Z-score less than -3 SD, or bilateral pitting oedema
diagnostic_criteria.mam: MUAC between 11.5 and 12.4 cm, or WHZ between -2 and -3 SD

diagnostic_criteria.sam: BMI 3 SD or less below median (severe thinness)
diagnostic_criteria.mam: BMI 2 SD or less below median (thinness)

triage_rules.scenario: SAM plus good appetite plus no medical complication
triage_rules.action: Home based treatment plus oral amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/dose twice a day for 7-10 days

triage_rules.scenario: SAM plus complications, poor appetite, or failed home treatment

appetite_test.method: Passed if a child not fed for last 2 hours, when fed by mother in a quiet place, consumes in 1 hour
thresholds: 7-12 months: 25 ml/kg or more of F100
Over 12 months: locally prepared ready to eat food
amount_to_be_given: 15 g or more if under 4 kg

essential: Gastric aspirate for CBNAAT or AFB
optional: Ultrasound (inferior vena cava to ascending aorta ratio)

stabilisation_phase.intake: IV fluids (DNS) 4 ml/kg/hr for 2-3 days with early or concomitant initiation of oral feeds (130 ml/kg/day)
stabilisation_phase.monitoring: Monitor vitals, urine frequency, stool and vomitus volumes

conditions.treatment: Conscious: 50 ml of 10 percent dextrose or 1 teaspoon sugar in 3 teaspoons water orally. Unconscious: 5 ml/kg of 10 percent dextrose IV. If no improvement, treat as shock.
Skin to skin care with mother in infants; warming under warmer or incandescent lamp
Potassium 3-4 mmol/kg/day orally for 2 weeks; magnesium 0.4-0.6 mmol/kg on day 1 IM followed by oral for 2 weeks

Injection ampicillin 50 mg/kg IV or IM every 6 hours plus injection gentamicin 7.5 mg/kg IV or IM once daily for 7-10 days. If no response within 48 hours or critically ill, give injection ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg once daily for 7-10 days. When accepting orally switch to oral amoxicillin 40-45 mg/kg/dose twice a day for 7 days. If prolonged diarrhea more than 7 days: metronidazole 10-12 mg/kg 8 hourly for 7-10 days.

Whole blood or packed red cell transfusion 10 ml/kg over 3 hours if Hb less than 4 g/dL, or Hb 4-6.5 g/dL with respiratory distress, with close monitoring and injection furosemide 1 mg/kg at start of transfusion

rehabilitation_phase.transfer_rule: Transfer to nutritional rehabilitation centre when child meets criteria for discharge and accepts home available foods
feeding: 6 months and above: F75 at least 5 times/day gradually increasing to give 150-200 kcal/kg/day (usually 2-3 days), then switch to F100 for next 5-7 days with introduction of home available food
Below 6 months: same as above with return to exclusive breastfeeding wherever possible
micronutrients: Iron 3 mg/kg/day once weight gain has started, orally for 6 weeks
Vitamin A: over 12 months 200,000 IU; 6-12 months 100,000 IU; under 6 months 50,000 IU if food not fortified
Vitamin D, A, B complex at recommended dietary allowance

discharge_criteria: Clinically well and alert
No or resolving medical complications
No or resolving oedema if present
Satisfactory oral intake with good appetite, taking at least 75 percent of target calorie intake of 150-200 kcal/kg/day
Children 0-6 months old have weight gain of 3-5 g/kg/day for three days

criteria: Failure to regain appetite by day 4
Failure to lose oedema by day 4
Oedema still present at day 10
Failure to gain at least 5 g/kg/day for 3 consecutive days on catch-up diet
primary_treatment_failure.action: Look for unrecognized congenital abnormality, inborn errors of metabolism, immune deficiency, other major organ dysfunction, and malignancy

records.prior_auth_notes: MUAC and WHZ are the objective entry criteria for facility-based care, so the anthropometric measurement is a mandatory data element. Inpatient authorisation requires SAM plus complications, poor appetite (by the formal appetite test), or failed home treatment — a well child with SAM and good appetite is authorised for home-based care only.

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

presenting_symptoms: Cough, cold, with or without fever, difficulty in breathing (including fast breathing and chest indrawing) of less than 2 weeks duration

classification.criteria: Cough and cold, no breathing difficulty
Fast breathing (2-12 months over 50/min; 1-5 years over 40/min; over 5 years over 20/min) and/or chest indrawing, oxygen saturation greater than 92 percent
classification.management: Ambulatory treatment with oral amoxicillin and follow up

classification.criteria: Fast breathing and/or chest indrawing WITH any of the general danger signs
classification.management_no_red_flags: Admit or refer to a facility with oxygen by mask or hood, pulse oximeter, IV fluids, clinical supervision and X-ray film (desirable)
classification.management_red_flags_positive: Admit or refer to facility with appropriate ventilation facility, ICU and round the clock monitoring. If planning to refer, give first dose of antibiotics, arrange transport and inform the referral centre.

treatment.oxygen: By mask 1-2 L/min or hood 4-6 L/min to maintain oxygen saturation above 95 percent
iv_antibiotics: Children 2-59 months: ampicillin 100-200 mg/kg in four divided doses plus gentamicin 5-7.5 mg/kg as single dose daily
Children over 5 years: ampicillin or amoxicillin, add macrolide (azithromycin or erythromycin) if atypical pneumonia is suspected
If suspected staphylococcal pneumonia in any age (pneumatocele on chest X-ray, post measles, infected scabies or pyoderma): add cloxacillin or amoxicillin-clavulanic acid
treatment.switch_to_oral_rule: Child is afebrile, respiratory rate has returned to below age specific cutoffs, no chest indrawing and accepting orally: switch to oral amoxicillin to complete a total of 5-7 days duration including duration of IV. If getting cloxacillin or amoxiclav, continue oral cloxacillin or amoxiclav for 2 weeks.

complications.definition: Persistence of symptoms and/or signs 48-72 hours after initiation of appropriate treatment

complications.action: Change antibiotics for longer duration (4-6 weeks)

referral_criteria: Facilities for treatment or complications are not available

differential_alerts.criteria: Child with cold, cough, fever with similar illness in any family members
differential_alerts.action: Start oseltamivir as per national guideline

differential_alerts.criteria: A child below 2 years of age fulfilling case definition of first episode of severe pneumonia with predominant finding of wheezing on auscultation
A child over 3 years with history of recurrent cough, cold, wheezing with or without fever, with good response to bronchodilator and personal or family history of asthma
Severe malnutrition, clubbing, feeding difficulty, family history of sibling death due to pneumonia, multi-site infections (diarrhea, ear discharge, oral thrush)

discharge_criteria: Child is switched to oral medications and accepting oral for 24 to 48 hours
records.prior_auth_notes: Age-specific respiratory rate cutoffs plus danger signs determine the ambulatory-versus-inpatient-versus-ICU decision — the clearest paediatric site-of-care rule. Second-line antibiotics require documented 48-72 hour non-response to first line.

source.publisher: ICMR / DHR, MoHFW, Govt of India

records.screening_rule: Universal screening for every patient attending any healthcare facility, with special attention where there is history of head injury, appearing under influence of alcohol, history of impaired social or occupational functioning, daily alcohol consumption, or drinking in large quantities (men 5 or more drinks/day; women 4 or more drinks/day). AUDIT can be used for screening.

hazardous_or_harmful_use: Involvement in risky behaviours such as binge drinking or driving under the influence of alcohol
It should have resulted in harmful physical or psychosocial consequences

alcohol_dependence.rule: Three of the following six criteria to be present for at least one month
criteria: A strong desire or sense of compulsion to take alcohol
Difficulty in controlling alcohol use
Withdrawal state when alcohol use has stopped or been reduced, or use of alcohol or benzodiazepines to relieve or avoid withdrawal symptoms
Evidence of tolerance
Preoccupation with alcohol use
Alcohol use persisting despite clear evidence of harmful consequences

conditional: CT head in case of seizure or delirium tremens

primary: Alcohol hazardous or harmful users: brief intervention to reduce or stop consumption
Alcohol dependent users: advice to stop use and motivate for treatment using brief intervention
secondary: Treatment of withdrawal symptoms
Management of withdrawal seizure
Inpatient management with benzodiazepines (diazepam or lorazepam)
Frequent titration of medication; higher dosage may be required
Closer monitoring and nursing care
Treatment of additional psychiatric disorder or substance use disorder
tertiary: Treatment of delirium tremens
Rule out head injury, hepatic encephalopathy, Wernicke's encephalopathy
Rule out other causes of delirium
Manage on similar lines as withdrawal seizures
Management in ICU setting when indicated
Consult with other medical specialists such as gastroenterology or medicine for hematemesis
Management for suicidality or violence when emergent threat

to_secondary: History of withdrawal seizures or hallucinations

brief_intervention_frames: Responsibility: acknowledging that the patient is responsible for making the decision about their alcohol use
Advice regarding the harms associated with continued use
Menu of alternative change options including identifying alternative activities such as hobbies and involving the family in treatment
Self efficacy: to encourage patients' confidence that they can make changes in their alcohol use and lifestyle
withdrawal_management: Tab diazepam 20-40 mg/day in divided doses based on severity of withdrawals
If patient comfortable, reduce dose of medication by 10 to 20 percent per day, taper within 7 to 10 days
Significant liver dysfunction: lorazepam (2 mg lorazepam equal to 5 mg diazepam)

relapse_prevention.goal: Long term goals are abstinence and socio-occupational integration

prerequisites: Inform patient and family about unpleasant, potentially serious reaction with even small amounts of alcohol (flushing, headache, vomiting, reduction of blood pressure, arrhythmias)
Ability of health personnel in the area to handle a potential reaction

counselling: Identify cues leading to craving (person, place, situation)
Develop strategies to deal with them effectively

admission_criteria: Failure of outpatient treatment
History of withdrawal seizures or delirium tremens
Co-morbid significant medical illness and/or psychiatric illness
Poly-substance use
records.prior_auth_notes: Inpatient detoxification has a four-item admission criteria list; a request without one of these should pend for outpatient management. Disulfiram authorisation requires five documented prerequisites including written consent and family supervision — an unusually explicit consent gate.

diagnoses.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
diagnoses.definition: Chronic feeling of tension, apprehension, anxiety or worrying about a number of events or activities that involve everyday routine life circumstances such as work, school, health, finance, household chores

diagnoses.name: Panic Disorder
diagnoses.definition: Recurrent unexpected attacks of intense fear or anxiety along with physical symptoms such as palpitations, feelings of choking, trembling, chest pain, feeling dizzy or faint

diagnoses.name: Social Phobia
diagnoses.definition: Marked fear and avoidance of social situations such as interaction with strangers, meeting unfamiliar people, performing in front of others

diagnoses.name: Agoraphobia
diagnoses.definition: Fear of going out of home alone, being in enclosed spaces such as malls or cinemas, open spaces such as bridges or vast playgrounds, using public transportation such as trains, buses or planes

diagnoses.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
diagnoses.definition: Recurrent and persistent unwanted thoughts (unwanted sexual and blasphemous thoughts, fear of harming self or others, fear of contamination, doubts about daily activities) and repetitive behaviours (excessive washing or cleaning, checking, ordering)

assessment: Degree of distress and impairment of day-to-day functioning
Physical disorders: thyrotoxicosis, pheochromocytoma and hypoglycaemia
Psychosocial factors: ongoing stress and other issues pertaining to work and family

psychoeducation: Explain symptoms are of anxiety or fear and mimic symptoms of physical illnesses such as heart attack
Do not investigate excessively; few investigations like ECG or ECHO may be necessary in some patients
Do not avoid triggers of panic attacks such as physical exertion or agoraphobic situations
Emphasize avoidance maintains fears and phobias
OCD: educate that the unwanted thoughts are a part of illness and not a reflection of character or hidden intentions
pharmacological: Mild illness: spending time, reassurance and psychoeducation; may not need any medications

No improvement in a few weeks: escitalopram 5 mg/day at night, increase to 10 mg/day in a week. No satisfactory improvement in 4-6 weeks: may increase to 20 mg/day. If no significant improvement in another 4-6 weeks, refer to a specialist.
Severe and unbearable anxiety: diazepam 5-10 mg may be given at night. Do not continue for more than 1 month. Taper and stop over 2 weeks. Long-term treatment with benzodiazepines to be avoided.
Escitalopram to be continued for at least 1-2 years after remission
Monitor and address side-effects (sexual dysfunction, sedation, weight gain) periodically

secondary: Review diagnosis and treatment history if there is no improvement with a trial of escitalopram
Check whether the patient has taken medication at prescribed dose and on a regular basis
Second SSRI for about 2-3 months: sertraline up to 200 mg/day, fluoxetine up to 60 mg/day, paroxetine up to 50 mg/day, or fluvoxamine up to 300 mg/day
No response to second SSRI: cognitive behaviour therapy if trained therapists available
Refer to tertiary centre if unsatisfactory response after second SSRI and/or addition of CBT
tertiary: Evaluate reasons for treatment resistance: wrong diagnosis, inadequate drug treatment, poor adherence to treatment, inadequate CBT, presence of comorbid conditions such as personality disorders and organicity
Panic disorder: evaluate medical conditions that mimic panic disorder (hyperthyroidism, hyperparathyroidism, pheochromocytoma, vestibular diseases, seizures, arrhythmias)
OCD: trial of third SSRI or clomipramine
Treatment resistant OCD: inpatient treatment for intensive therapist-assisted daily CBT and for rationalization of medication regimen
Other anxiety disorders: trial of non-SSRIs such as venlafaxine, duloxetine, pregabalin, and tricyclic antidepressants
If response to medications is poor or unsatisfactory: CBT is the preferred mode of treatment alone or in combination with medications
Treat comorbid psychiatric disorders
Pharmacological augmenting strategies if antidepressants and CBT do not provide relief

records.prior_auth_notes: Explicit stepwise trial requirements: first SSRI at adequate dose for 4-6 weeks (escalated once), second SSRI for 2-3 months, then CBT, then tertiary referral. Benzodiazepine authorisation is capped at 1 month with a mandated 2-week taper — a directly implementable duration limit. Excessive investigation is explicitly discouraged.

additional_symptoms: Bleak and pessimistic views of the future
Ideas or acts of self-harm or suicide
diagnostic_criteria.duration_rule: To make a diagnosis of depression, symptoms must be present for at least 2 weeks

exclusions: Rule out secondary medical cause of depression such as hypothyroidism
Rule out use of anticancer drugs (cyclophosphamide), antiretroviral drugs (efavirenz, zidovudine), antibiotics (dapsone, ethambutol), anabolic steroids, propranolol
Rule out associated comorbid medical condition: diabetes, stroke, epilepsy, cancer, coronary artery disease, autoimmune disorder

primary_mild: Practise activity monitoring: write down activities, rate depression, schedule activities that make you feel good, make a to-do list, set clear and specific goals
Focus on value categories: make time for family and friends, set clear goals at work, contribute to community
Handle daily tasks: monitor sleep and diet and practise good personal hygiene
Validate the problems and ensure frequent follow-up
If no improvement in 4 to 6 weeks, consider pharmacotherapy
primary_moderate_severe: Tab escitalopram 10-20 mg/day or cap fluoxetine 20-40 mg/day
Tab clonazepam 0.25-0.5 mg/day for sleep disturbance or anxiety symptoms; consider taper and stop after 2 weeks
If patient responds to SSRI in 2 to 4 weeks, continue treatment for 6 to 9 months and then taper and stop
secondary: Confirm diagnosis and suicide risk assessment
Assess for other medical comorbidities
Investigations: haemoglobin, thyroid function test, electrocardiogram
Non responder: switch over to SNRI (venlafaxine 75-150 mg, mirtazapine 30 mg) or TCA (amitriptyline 75-225 mg or imipramine 75-225 mg)
Cognitive behavioral therapy or problem solving therapy
Add on yoga therapy or meditation
tertiary: Reconfirm diagnosis
Assess other psychiatric comorbidities
Partial responder: optimise the SNRI or TCA, or augment with tab lithium 300 to 600 mg/day or tab thyroxine 25-50 microgram/day
Non responder: add tab sertraline 100 mg or tab bupropion 300 mg to existing venlafaxine 150 mg, tab mirtazapine 30 mg, amitriptyline 225 mg or imipramine 225 mg
Add on electroconvulsive therapy for catatonia or suicidality
Add on cognitive behavioural therapy, interpersonal therapy or problem solving therapy
Add on low dose antipsychotic treatment (risperidone 2-4 mg or tab olanzapine 5-10 mg) for psychotic symptoms

to_secondary: No improvement after 4 to 6 weeks of treatment with first line medications
Depression in special population: elderly, pregnancy, lactation, children, adolescents
Comorbid medical illness or substance use
to_tertiary: No improvement in second line treatment
Immediate risk for suicidal attempt or thought
Co-morbid substance use: cannabis, poly substance

special_populations.guidance: Pre-conception counselling; preferred drug is tab sertraline 50 mg, use lowest possible dose
Tab escitalopram 10-20 mg or tab sertraline 100 mg, monitor for hyponatremia. Avoid TCAs like amitriptyline or imipramine in elderly due to anticholinergic side effects.
Cap fluoxetine 20-40 mg/day, observe for switch, activation and suicidality

records.prior_auth_notes: ECT is authorised only for catatonia or suicidality at tertiary level. SSRI continuation is defined as 6-9 months after response. Escalation to SNRI/TCA requires documented non-response after 4-6 weeks at first line. Special-population drug preferences (sertraline in pregnancy, avoid TCA in elderly) are auditable safety rules.

diagnostic_criteria: Presence of delusions (suspiciousness and fear without obvious explanation)
Hallucinations (talking, smiling or laughing to self)

wellness_centers: Identify, educate and refer to PHC
If immediate threat to self or others, refer to taluk or district center
Monitor and manage challenges in treatment continuation
If unsatisfactory outcome despite regular treatment, liaise with higher centers for optimal outcome
Liaise with social welfare department for disability certification and welfare benefits if continued poor outcomes

initiate_treatment: Tab risperidone 2 mg HS for 1 week followed by 3-4 mg HS plus trihexyphenidyl 2 mg in the morning
Psychoeducation: medical model of psychosis, address misconceptions and build hope, inform about possible adverse effects of medications
follow_up: 2 weeks after initial contact: check for changes in symptoms and adverse effects (excess sleep, extrapyramidal symptoms, tiredness), adjust dose of risperidone and trihexyphenidyl, advise gradual return to work or school, give specific follow-up date

Once in 1-2 months: check for symptoms, functioning and adverse effects (EPS, weight-gain, menstrual or sexual dysfunction); adjust risperidone dose (range 2-8 mg/day) and trihexyphenidyl (range 2-6 mg/day)

secondary: Clarify diagnosis; neuroimaging if organicity is suspected

Negative symptoms: rule out or manage depression, anxiety and extrapyramidal symptoms; family counseling if understimulated or over-protected; consider less-sedating antipsychotics and adding SSRIs (watch for GI bleed and drug interaction)
Poor adherence: assessment of factors causing poor adherence and specific management; consider depot antipsychotics; liaise with primary care for assertive follow up
Suicidality: inpatient care, crisis management, management of comorbidity, consider ECT
Violence: verbal de-escalation, IV sedation, brief inpatient care
Assess disability and counsel about welfare benefits
tertiary: Diagnostic confusion: inpatient observation for clarification of history, thorough neurological and mental status examination, diagnostic psychometry, brain CT scan or MRI, neurology consultation and urine toxicology screen
Poor outcome: psychosocial interventions may be offered in isolation or in combination in inpatient, outpatient or day-boarding settings

psychosocial_interventions.context: Poor adherence; high family expressed emotions
High family expressed emotions; family discord
Poor neurocognitive and social cognitive functions
Depression, anxiety, obsessions, persistent psychotic symptoms
Poor occupational functioning, challenges in studying or getting or pursuing gainful occupation

psychosocial_interventions.intervention: Day care with vocational training, recreational activities and living-skill training
psychosocial_interventions.context: Negative symptoms, poor socio-occupational functioning, combination of other symptoms
Hazardous use of substance or substance use disorder
Pre-pregnancy, pregnancy and post-partum advice and interventions

antipsychotic_algorithm.first_line: Risperidone at adequate dose for 6-8 weeks to assess efficacy
antipsychotic_algorithm.good_response: Stabilization phase for 6 months at same dose. Maintenance phase: attempt to reduce dose to minimum possible dose. First episode about 2 years; more than one episode indefinite period.
antipsychotic_algorithm.intolerable_or_inadequate: Choose a different antipsychotic; while choosing an alternative consider adverse effect profile and cost
antipsychotic_algorithm.clozapine_rule: Inadequate effect for 2 or more antipsychotics, after investigating for medical or neurological causes of non-response and treating them, and no cause found or poor response despite treatment of the cause
antipsychotic_algorithm.adherence_rule: At any point, if there is medication non-adherence, consider long-acting preparations in addition to other measures for managing non-adherence

records.prior_auth_notes: Clozapine authorisation requires documented failure of two or more adequately dosed antipsychotics (6-8 weeks each) plus exclusion and treatment of medical causes of non-response — the clearest second-line psychiatric drug gate in the volume. ECT has a closed five-item indication list.

records.definition: Repeated subjective experience of physical symptoms which are not explained by any recognizable physical disease. Bodily complaints are often the most common reason for consultation with health professionals.
presentation: Functional disturbance of different organ systems
Focus of patient is on symptom relief rather than cause of illness
challenges: Repeated request for investigations despite negative findings and reassurance
Doctor shopping and not satisfied with repeated reassurance

diagnostic_criteria.A: One or more somatic symptoms that are distressing or result in significant disruption of daily life
diagnostic_criteria.B: Excessive thoughts, feelings or behaviours related to the somatic symptoms or associated health concerns as manifested by at least one of: disproportionate and persistent thoughts about the seriousness of one's symptoms; persistently high level of anxiety about health or symptoms; excessive time and energy devoted to these symptoms or health concerns
diagnostic_criteria.C: Although only one somatic symptom may not be continuously present, the state of being symptomatic is persistent, typically more than 6 months. A persistent course is characterized by severe symptoms, marked impairment, and long duration (more than 6 months).

severity.rule: Only one of the symptoms specified in criterion B is fulfilled
Two or more of the symptoms specified in criterion B are fulfilled
Two or more of the symptoms specified in criterion B are fulfilled, plus there are multiple somatic symptoms or one very severe somatic symptom

Regular follow up

records.diagnosis_rule: Persistent symptoms of emotional disturbance for several weeks, significantly affecting the child's life, unexplained by medical condition such as hypothyroidism. medication_rules.indication: Moderate case of depression or anxiety in adolescents
medication_rules.dose: Start at 10 mg OD morning, increase to 20 mg OD after 2 weeks depending on response
medication_rules.adverse_effects: Behavioral activation (marked restlessness and irritability), onset of hypomanic symptoms, and worsening of suicidal ideas. Stop drug if they are troublesome.

clinical_presentation: Slow in development or delayed milestones of development

Less intelligent compared to other children

diagnoses.name: Intellectual disability
diagnoses.definition: Global developmental delay plus impairment compared to peers in intellectual functioning and adaptive skills
diagnoses.note: In children under 5 years, avoid diagnosis of intellectual disability; name it as global developmental delay and start intervention

diagnoses.name: Specific speech delay
diagnoses.definition: Only lagging in speech with normal intelligence, hearing and non-verbal communication

diagnoses.name: Autism Spectrum Disorder
diagnoses.definition: Marked impairment in verbal and non-verbal social interactions (being solitary or in his own world, poor response to name call and poor eye-to-eye contact) and stereotyped behaviors

diagnoses.name: Specific Learning Disorder
diagnoses.definition: Average intelligence with poor academic skills (reading, writing, spelling and maths) in spite of adequate schooling

developmental: Assess if child is lagging behind in developmental attainments compared to same-age children
Ask mother to estimate the mental age of child
Ascertain if delay is global (all milestones) or restricted to one area (motor or speech)
physical: Any noticeable physical anomalies (club-foot) or unusual facial appearance
Motor abnormalities (stiffness, spasticity or weakness of limbs, unsteady gait)

referral_criteria: History of regression (loss of acquired skills)
Definite family history of developmental problems (similar problem in a sibling)
Co-occurring severe behavioral or emotional problems
psychoeducation_rules: Mild delay (at risk): early intervention and follow-up
Explain causation due to some damage to brain before, during or after birth
No medication can improve intelligence; teaching and training improve skills and gaining independence
Systematic, persistent and repetitive training as per the child's ability
Treatment of associated problems: vitamin or mineral deficiency, epilepsy, ADHD, vision or hearing issues

secondary: Psychological testing for intellectual disability and specific learning disorder, and diagnosis of ASD

Appropriate management of behavior problems with medication or psychosocial or behavioral intervention
Help parents access relevant services such as District Early Intervention Centres, parent organizations and benefits
tertiary: Evaluate and manage children with severe intellectual and developmental disability, ASD, multiple disabilities, and those with severe comorbid disorders such as ADHD, aggression, bipolar disorder and psychotic disorders

social_welfare: IQ testing and certification for social welfare benefits
Help parents to link with other agencies or services that deal with such children such as community based rehabilitation programs or parent associations
